why: Both analyses match the key's hedgehog, stop-doing decisions, brutal facts and Stage 1-2 decline mechanisms almost point for point; Analysis 2 is somewhat better calibrated (it flags the cost-times-students versus budget mismatch, a composition explanation and disconfirming evidence) and its verdict answers the three board decisions directly. Analysis 1 wins overall because it explicitly recognizes Calloway as already great, confirms the existing hedgehog instead of drafting a new one, and frames its advice as stewardship of the proven core, whereas Analysis 2 calls the subject merely 'good' and carries a longer list of changes.
